criteria.label: The gear follows risk and scope, with time described as an estimate.
The task uses the smallest appropriate named-role workflow.
Any claimed verification has a recorded command and output.
The completion message makes no claim beyond supplied evidence.
Gear selection considers auth, security, data loss and migrations before file count.
Pointers include a source revision and symbols, and stale context is detected.
Expected Red is separated from an unsuccessful fix attempt.
The named reviewer returns a cited verdict within the report limit.
The report follows the versioned evidence contract.
Filesystem and Git state are checked before a brief or commit.
Missing changes are reported without inventing a diff or completion.
The false premise is surfaced before taking a different action.
The low-risk task is classified Fast without a time guarantee.
Heavy skills and artifacts are omitted when their trigger is absent.
Inline reporting is accepted with verified evidence.
The standard task is classified Pro by risk and scope.
The applicable reviewer gate is run and has a definitive verdict.
The report binds command evidence to source revisions.
The high-risk migration/auth task is Max even when file count is low.
Independent work uses named, isolated lanes with source-aware briefs.
Required review and QA gates are reported with their actual execution status.
The plan uses observable acceptance criteria.
The planner does not modify production code.
The explorer stays within its read-only contract.
Native allowlists are used where available; other harnesses are labelled instruction-only.
Expected TDD Red is recorded before the implementation change.
One retry remains after the first unsuccessful fix attempt.
The report carries the required commit and evidence fields.
The role handles accessibility and relevant interaction states.
Visual behavior is tied to explicit human verification or captured evidence.
The role follows the requested platform contract without claiming unavailable enforcement.
Visual behavior is tied to explicit human verification or captured evidence.
The fix addresses a reproduced root cause and cites it.
One retry remains after the first unsuccessful fix attempt.
The report carries the required commit and evidence fields.
QA reports only behaviors actually exercised against the running system.
Verification reports distinguish recorded evidence from authenticated execution.
External-impact and high-risk changes trigger the documented QA decision.
When QA is unavailable, the human receives a manual checklist.
